title: Eviction policy v1 for KV cache (victim selection + fairness) + pathological tests
creator: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Context
- KV cache fragmentation + allocation churn under bursty mixed-length traffic is driving tail latency spikes and occasional allocation failures.
- Compaction reduces fragmentation, but eviction behavior still matters: under pressure we must choose victims deterministically and fairly, and we must avoid pathological thrash / starvation that makes p99 worse.

Goal
Define and implement eviction policy v1 for KV cache blocks/segments that is:
- Scheduler-aware: respects tenant tier / SLA class and avoids starvation.
- Correct under concurrency: never evicts memory still referenced by in-flight decode/prefill kernels.
- Predictable: stable victim selection with clear ranking and explicit caps.
- Testable: includes correctness tests + adversarial/pathological simulations.

Non-goals
- Perfect global optimality. This is the safe baseline to unblock canary; future iterations can add more sophisticated heuristics.
- Changing model semantics or attention behavior.

Proposed policy (v1)
We evict at the granularity of a KV “segment” (allocator blocks grouped by request/sequence). Eviction is triggered by allocation pressure (allocator cannot satisfy request, or fragmentation/pressure signals cross threshold; triggers are implemented in ENG-2847 but victim selection lives here).

Definitions
- Request classes:
  - tier: {dedicated_enterprise, hosted_enterprise, hosted_standard, internal}
  - sla_class: {latency_sensitive, throughput, best_effort}
- Sequence states:
  - ACTIVE_DECODE: participating in decode loop (highest protection)
  - ACTIVE_PREFILL: in-flight prefill kernels / awaiting completion (protected)
  - IDLE: request admitted but not currently scheduled this tick (eligible with penalty)
  - COMPLETED: can be freed immediately (not “evicted”)
- Pinned/Protected segments:
  - Any segment referenced by an in-flight kernel (CUDA stream not yet synchronized) is non-evictable.
  - Prefix-cache “pinned” segments (if enabled) are non-evictable unless explicit override flag is set (not in v1; default is protect).

Victim scoring
Eligible victims are sequences/segments in state IDLE only (v1 conservative), plus ACTIVE_DECODE only if we are in “hard pressure” mode (see below).
We compute a victim score; higher score = more eligible:
1) Tier weight (primary): lower tier evicts first
   - internal: 0 (never evict, instead backpressure; exception: test env)
   - dedicated_enterprise: 1
   - hosted_enterprise: 2
   - hosted_standard: 3
   - best_effort: 4
2) Age / recency:
   - last_scheduled_ms (older = more eligible)
3) Remaining work heuristic (avoid evicting near-complete):
   - estimated_remaining_tokens (higher = more eligible)
4) KV footprint:
   - kv_bytes (larger = slightly more eligible to quickly relieve pressure, bounded)
5) Fairness guard:
   - per-tenant eviction debt/credit: tenants that have been evicted more recently get a temporary protection window to avoid repeated hits.

Hard pressure mode
If allocator reports allocation failure for a mandatory segment (or OOM risk indicator crosses critical threshold), we allow eviction of ACTIVE_DECODE sequences in lowest tiers with strict limits:
- Only from best_effort and hosted_standard.
- Max 1 eviction per scheduling tick per tenant.
- Requires scheduler acknowledgement via cache_pressure=CRITICAL (hook added in ENG-2846).

Explicit invariants (must hold)
- Never evict from a sequence with in-flight kernels (stream sync / refcount > 0).
- Never evict dedicated_enterprise / hosted_enterprise in normal pressure mode.
- No starvation: if any best_effort/hosted_standard IDLE sequences exist, we must not evict higher tier.
- Determinism: for a fixed eligible set + metrics snapshot, victim ordering is stable.

API / integration points
- Allocator exposes: list_eligible_eviction_candidates() returning candidate IDs + metadata snapshot (tier, last_scheduled_ms, kv_bytes, remaining_tokens_est, tenant_id, pinned, inflight_refcount).
- Scheduler passes cache_pressure signal: {NONE, SOFT, HARD, CRITICAL} (added in ENG-2846; for now stub with config).
- Eviction returns: victim_id, bytes_freed, reason (normal_pressure | hard_pressure | critical_pressure).

Implementation plan
1) Implement EvictionPolicyV1 class in runtime cache manager:
   - Candidate filter (pinned/protected/inflight)
   - Score computation with bounded contributions + tie-breakers (tenant_id then request_id)
   - Per-tenant debt tracking (sliding window) with decay
2) Add a lightweight simulator harness:
   - Generates sequences with mixed lengths and burst arrivals
   - Applies scheduler ticks, pressure signals, admissions, and evictions
   - Asserts invariants and produces summary metrics (evictions per tier, fairness index)
3) Add unit + stress tests (see below)
4) Wire structured logging for eviction decisions:
   - victim selection trace with score breakdown
   - include tenant_id hash, tier, pressure mode, inflight_refcount, pinned

Test plan (required)
Correctness (unit)
- test_never_evict_inflight: candidate with inflight_refcount>0 is never selected
- test_tier_precedence: if any best_effort candidates exist, do not evict hosted_enterprise/dedicated in normal pressure
- test_deterministic_tiebreak: stable ordering with identical scores
- test_fairness_debt: repeated evictions rotate across tenants given equivalent eligibility

Pathological / adversarial (simulator)
- burst_mixed_lengths_thrashing: alternating long/short requests, ensure eviction rate doesn’t oscillate > threshold and no single tenant dominates evictions
- long_context_low_tier_under_pressure: ensure hard pressure mode only activates under CRITICAL and remains capped
- single_tenant_hot_loop: ensure eviction debt prevents same tenant from being hit every tick when others are eligible
- pinned_prefix_cache_interaction: pinned sequences never selected; ensure policy degrades to backpressure when only pinned remain

Acceptance criteria
- All invariants above enforced by tests.
- Simulator produces consistent fairness metrics (eviction share within ±20% of offered-load share for equal-tier tenants under sustained SOFT/HARD pressure).
- No evictions of enterprise tiers in SOFT/HARD modes in simulator runs.
- Logging present and sampled (rate-limited) for canary debugging.

Links / references
- Design doc: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kv-cache-compaction-improvements-design-v1
- ADR: confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0129-eviction-policy-scheduler-contract
- Related tickets: ENG-2844 (allocator refactor), ENG-2846 (scheduler contract), ENG-2847 (triggers/budgets)

Notes / open questions
- Should we allow eviction of ACTIVE_DECODE in HARD (not just CRITICAL) for best_effort? Current proposal is CRITICAL-only for safety.
- How to estimate remaining_tokens cheaply and consistently across model families (fallback: use generated_tokens so far + max_tokens).
- Whether to treat multi-seq requests as atomic eviction units (v1: atomic per-request to simplify correctness).
